old_caption: The video captures a close-up view of a sparkler being lit against a backdrop of blue, wavy, fabric-like material. The sparkler, positioned centrally, emits bright, fiery sparks that radiate outward in all directions. These sparks vary in size and intensity, creating a dynamic and mesmerizing visual effect. The blue background, which appears to be a textured, flowing surface, provides a stark contrast to the vivid orange and yellow hues of the sparks. As the sparkler burns, the sparks continue to flicker and dance, illuminating the scene with a warm glow. The overall atmosphere is one of celebration or festivity, enhanced by the vibrant colors and the continuous movement of the sparks. There are no other objects or characters present in the video, focusing solely on the interaction between the sparkler and its surroundings.

caption: The video captures a close-up of a lit sparkler held at an angle against a deep-blue, layered ribbon-like backdrop. The thin dark stick runs from the lower-left toward the upper-center, terminating in a bright white-yellow burning tip that throws a starburst of glowing sparks in every direction. Throughout the excerpt the tip's core flickers, sometimes flaring into a larger white blob and sometimes tightening. Individual sparks streak outward and vanish at varying positions around it, while the rod tilts slightly and the tip drifts a little near the upper-center, consistent with small handheld movements rather than any deliberate gesture. Falling sparks and short glowing trails appear and disappear lower in the frame, and a soft orange glow spot persists on the right side of the background. The blue ribbons themselves remain essentially stationary, holding the same positions from the first frame to the last.

not ground truth. Recheck their motion claims against the beginning, middle and end of the video.
You receive the original WISA caption's stylistic profile, without its possibly wrong facts.

Distinguish an already ongoing process from a new event actually visible within this excerpt.
Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.

"length_note":"empty unless materially shorter/longer than the requested style reference"}.
